# Performance baseline — 2026-10-30

## Status: plan 001 BLOCKED on deferred UI captures; plans 002–003 DONE; plan 004 REJECTED

Plan 001 microbenchmarks implemented and run twice. The user approved the proposed
microbenchmark targets on 2026-10-30 and authorized plan 002, explicitly deferring
UI captures and prohibiting shared-runtime restart or Library switching. Plan 002
completed after the user approved the tied-recency adjustment (details below).
Plan 003 is complete with measured query improvements. Plan 004 is finalized as
REJECTED with user approval: keep the exact scan. Repository gates passed; four
benchmark phases remain explicitly incomplete. See its decision report. End-to-end captures remain deferred. Shared runtime was not
started, stopped, restarted, or switched; no personal Library was opened.
No production behavior, dependencies, native ABI, or CI configuration changed.

## Environment and method

- Base commit: `e88675ff51e4e22a05b87ab6e79553c69d6c1956`, branch
  `perf/library-performance`; benchmark files are working-tree additions.
- Apple M4, macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64; Electron 44.4.0 / its Node 24.21.0.
- Run 1 began 08:29:52 UTC; run 2 began 08:31:23 UTC, 2026-10-30.
  Durations: 79.60s / 79.03s. Both: 2 files, 39 tests passed, no skips.
- Each run emitted 120 JSON records: 84 query cases and 36 pool cases.
  All records include 5 warm-ups and 30 measured samples.
- Exact commands and capture protocol:
  [performance runbook](../docs/contributing/performance.md).
- Default Vitest file parallelism: query and pool workers competed. No other
  checks/builds were launched during either run. A process-name snapshot before
  run 2 showed editor helpers, Node processes and nine vitest-vscode processes.
  Their activity, shared app activity, power and thermal state were not controlled.
  No processes were killed. A quiet rerun requires runtime-owner coordination.
- Query fixtures are in-memory native SQLite, not disk startup. Pool fixtures
  have no DOM, persistence, real IPC, or rendering. Query fixture setup and pool
  reset costs are excluded from operation timing and reported separately.
- First/next queries use limit 250. Next-page cases are not applicable for
  N=1k keyword (100 matches), N=1k selective (10), and N=10k selective (100),
  for both sorts and both pin sets: 12 combinations have no valid next cursor.
  All remaining matrix combinations executed; no timeout or ABI blocks.
- p50/p95 are nearest-rank statistics. Raw samples are preserved below.
  Memory is test-process RSS/heap/external snapshots, not whole-app usage, peaks,
  retained allocations, or GPU memory. No forced GC.

CI gates without a coordinated quiet measurement window.

## Microbenchmark targets — approved 2026-10-30

These are optimization hypotheses based on this machine's microbenchmarks, not
product latency promises or pass/fail gates:

- Plan 002: one optimistic store publication per nonempty bulk operation and at
  most one additional rollback publication. For N=50k/K=1000, propose p95 <=50%
  of run 2 for each operation (rating 170.43ms, trash 175.56ms, purge 101.44ms,
  rollback 336.78ms), measured with the same protocol. Record all smaller cases
  too; agree tolerances after a quiet repeat.
- Plan 003: for unpinned all-Library recency, propose >=25% p95 reduction from
  run 2 at N=50k (first <=18.16ms, next <=23.22ms), with exact counts/order
  preserved. Pinned/title/keyword/folder paths must retain correctness; their
  timing tolerance needs a quiet repeat rather than treating outliers as budget.
- Plan 004: approve the isolated SQL measurement protocol first. No semantic
  latency target is justified yet; cold encoder, warm encoder, and SQL must be
  measured independently before agreeing targets.
- Startup, first usable Library, scroll/filter responsiveness, bulk-renderer
  long tasks and post-idle whole-app memory: **not measured; no budget proposed**.
- Encoder cold start, warm execution and isolated vector SQL: **not measured**.

Approval: **explicitly granted by the user on 2026-10-30**: “Approve the proposed
microbenchmark targets. Proceed with plan 002, but defer UI captures and don’t
restart or switch the shared runtime.” These microbenchmark targets use the Apple
M4 baseline above; no stable CI runner or CI timing gate was approved. UI capture
permission remains withheld. Plan 004 still requires its own spike approval gate.

## Plan 002 progress and STOP evidence — 2026-10-30

Historical checkpoint: resolved by subsequent user approval and the completed
implementation recorded below.

- Drift check: no committed or uncommitted changes to plan 002 production inputs.
- Added characterization coverage for all bulk operation kinds, duplicate and cold
  IDs, empty selections, rating exclusion, success, rejection, keyed/snapshot
  consistency, and dirty IDs. Original behavior passed all 26 mutation tests.
- Added `pool.bulkDelete`: one publication/revision and one dirty notification
  for present IDs, no-op for empty/all-missing input, stable survivor ordering.
  Three pool tests pass. This primitive is not yet wired into bulk mutations.
- Reviewed dirty consumers: live facets handles ID batches and enrichment schedules
  scans for ID batches. Neither requires intermediate per-Save states.
- Added a tied-timestamp rejected-purge characterization: select one of two Saves
  with savedAt=20, purge it, reject persistence. Existing single upserts leave
  the surviving Save before the restored Save: `["survivor", "selected"]`.
- A temporary probe replacing only rollback's per-Save upserts with
  `pool.bulkUpsert(before)` failed that test, producing
  `["selected", "survivor"]`. The bulk fast path permits a new Save with
  recency equal to the head and prepends it; the single path performs stable
  recency sorting over Map insertion order.
- The experimental rollback replacement was reverted. No failing test or changed
  bulk mutation behavior is retained. Plan 002 is BLOCKED under its explicit
  “one batch changes tied recency ordering” STOP condition.
- Recommended follow-up requiring approval: adjust the bulk-upsert fast path so
  newly inserted Saves tied with the head fall back to the existing stable sort;
  characterize tied ordering for ordinary bulk upserts and purge rollback before
  continuing. This would alter the current bulk-insertion tie behavior, so it is
  not silently included in the optimization.
- No post-batching performance claim is made. The original baseline remains the
  comparison reference. Repository-wide gates have not been rerun for this
  partial plan; the plan 001 gate results above are historical.

## Plan 002 completed — 2026-10-30

The user explicitly approved the tied-recency adjustment after the STOP above.
New Saves tied with the existing head now use stable sorting instead of the
prepend fast path, matching single-upsert ordering. Ordinary tied inserts,
updates, strictly newer inserts, and rejected purge are covered.

Bulk application now uses one bulk upsert or bulk deletion. Rollback restores
changed pre-operation objects in one batch; identical object references are
excluded, matching the old single-upsert no-op behavior. Cold IDs still reach
main; non-optimistic operations and rating eligibility are unchanged. The prior
rollback overwrite policy for intervening edits is preserved, not redesigned.

### Measurement and comparison

- Base commit remains e88675ff; measured working tree includes plan 002 changes.
- Same Apple M4 / Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 / Electron 44.4.0 / Node 24.21.0.
- Plan 002 bulk-only command: 09:50:03 local, 5.94s, 36 tests and 36 JSON records.
- Supplementary command matching plan 001's two-file invocation: 09:50:10 local,
  86.68s, 39 tests and 120 records. Bulk records from both runs are retained below.
- Both commands used POND_BENCH_LIBRARY=1 and ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, five warm-ups
  and thirty measured samples per case, identical fixture/reset/timing boundaries.
  The only benchmark change adds exact publication assertions after timing.
- No checks/builds overlapped these runs. Background activity and thermals remain
  uncontrolled. The two-file run retains query-worker competition for comparison;
  because the optimized bulk run finishes sooner, overlap duration necessarily
  differs. These are microbenchmarks, not renderer frame or whole-app measurements.
- Every changing optimistic phase published exactly once; rollback published
  exactly once more, for all N/K combinations.
- All four approved N=50k/K=1000 p95 targets passed in both post-change runs.
  Comparable two-file p95: rating 3.29ms <=170.43ms, trash 4.04ms <=175.56ms,
  purge 6.46ms <=101.44ms, rollback 9.02ms <=336.78ms.
- Small K can be slower despite the large-K win: unordered K=100 updates now
  perform one full recency sort; some noisy K=1 samples also increased.
  The approved targets concern K=1000, not a claim that every workload improves.
  The plan explicitly accepts one O(N log N) batch initially; further tuning
  is not included here.

## Plan 003 completed — 2026-10-30

### Scope and evidence

The user authorized plan 003 after approving its microbenchmark targets. Drift
checks found no changes to the query/schema inputs. Existing plan 001/002 work
was preserved; no schema, indexes, IPC contracts, renderer query sessions, count
cache, dependencies, or CI configuration changed. Shared runtime untouched.

Drizzle's supported logger captured the actual emitted SQL and bound parameters,
then the same synthetic SQLite connection executed EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. The
diagnostic matrix has 72 cases at N=10k: savedAt/title, asc/desc, zero/three pins,
all/broad/selective scope, and first/next/all-IDs queries. Limit 25 permits real
second pages even in the 100-result selective scope. The original 84-case
N=1k/10k/50k limit-250 matrix is retained for baseline comparison.

Before changing production code, the unpinned savedAt descending plan showed
correlated json_each pin lookups and USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY. At N=10k,
first/next p95 was 9.87/7.36ms in the diagnostic run; raw prepared row replays
were 10.11/6.41ms versus count replays 1.74/0.74ms. These independent samples
include noise and are not additive slices of the overall timer. This supported
removing per-row pin work, not an assumption that an index was absent.

### Implementation and compatibility

Only unpinned savedAt (including the default sort) uses the new fast path:
constant unpinned rank, direct savedAt/descending-ID ordering, and a simplified
cursor predicate. Descending uses a lexicographic savedAt/ID comparison;
ascending keeps descending ID tie-breaking. Page/all-IDs share ordering.
Nullable, title, manual, random, and pinned sorts retain the general path.
Nonstandard cursor ranks and null cursor values retain the general predicate.

The sort signature, returned cursor fields/rank convention, Library validation,
and exact count inside the page transaction are unchanged. Fifty-five native
query tests passed both before and after implementation. Added coverage includes
both directions, repeated timestamps, nullable ratings, scoped-out pins,
deleted/incomplete Saves, empty results, full page traversal against all-IDs,
legacy-format cursors, and exact totals after intervening insert/trash writes.

After optimization, the unpinned savedAt query plans have no pin-rank subqueries.
**They still use saves_status_idx and a temporary ORDER BY B-tree in this
unanalyzed synthetic fixture.** The existing saves_saved_at_id_idx remains
present and untouched; this is not a demonstrated index-scan optimization.
No ANALYZE, index hint, migration, or count caching was introduced.

For N=10k unpinned savedAt descending diagnostics, first/next/all-IDs p95 became
2.25/2.26/4.45ms versus 9.87/7.36/6.13ms. Count replay p95 stayed around
0.65–0.68ms and row replay p95 was 1.50–1.76ms. Exact counts and remaining sorting
are possible future investigation areas, not additional changes in this plan.

### Repeatability and approved target

Same base commit e88675ff plus the documented working-tree changes; Apple M4,
Darwin 25.6.0 arm64, Electron 44.4.0 / Node 24.21.0. Five warm-ups, thirty measured
samples per case. Three sequential native query-only commands (no checks/builds
overlapped them):

```sh
POND_BENCH_LIBRARY=1 ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 pnpm --filter @pond/desktop exec electron node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/main/core/library-performance-benchmark.test.ts
```

- Before: 10:01:50 local, 111.09s; 3 tests passed, 156 records.
- After: 10:05:35 local, 96.47s; 3 tests passed, 156 records.
- Independent after repeat: 10:07:45 local, 99.47s; 3 tests passed, 156 records.
- Background activity, power/thermal state and shared-runtime load were not
  controlled. Unlike plan 001's two-file baseline, these are query-only runs.
  The fresh before/after matrix uses matching invocations and instrumentation.
- Raw count/row stage timings replay prepared SQL outside the production-call
  timer, include raw SQLite materialization, and exclude prepare/Drizzle mapping.
  They are separately labeled diagnostics, not direct instrumentation of stages.
- No real startup, disk access, IPC, hydration, UI rendering or semantic encoder
  latency is measured. Process-memory snapshots remain worker-only, not app memory.
- After measurements, lint-only cleanup renamed the diagnostic JSON field
  `shape` to `queryKind` and replaced an empty-array type assertion with an
  explicit number[][] annotation. Historical raw records retain `shape`.

At N=50k unpinned all-Library savedAt descending:

| Page | Original plan 001 run 2 p95 | Fresh before p95 | After p95 | Repeat p95 | Approved ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First | 24.21ms | 23.15ms | 12.96ms | 13.46ms | 18.16ms |
| Next | 30.96ms | 29.15ms | 13.35ms | 14.49ms | 23.22ms |

Both runs pass both approved ceilings. Against the fresh before baseline,
the measured saving is approximately 42–44% for the first page and 50–54% for
the next page. These are query microbenchmarks, not equivalent UI latency claims.

Unchanged paths are not promised improvements: for example N=10k title,
three pins, all scope, first-page p95 rose above 7.6ms in the first after run.
All cases are reported below, including slower/noisy cases. No general-path
timing threshold was approved; no statistical significance is claimed.

### Verification

- Native query suite: 55/55 before and after; final combined native gate
  db/vec-index/query: 63/63 tests, no skips.
- Initial pnpm check rejected a diagnostic variable name and an unnecessary
  type assertion. Repaired without weakening rules; final pnpm check exit 0,
  28 tasks successful, desktop 4692 passed / 44 skipped.
- pnpm build exit 0; all five size budgets passed.
- git diff --check passed. In-scope production change is library-query.ts;
  tests, benchmark, report and index complete the plan 003 scope.
- No commits/pushes. Plan 004 has not started and retains its approval gate.

## Plan 004 partial spike — 2026-10-30

Historical checkpoint; the approved finalization below supersedes its BLOCKED status.

[Vector retrieval decision and raw results](vector-retrieval-decision.md).

- Real native adapter tests: 31/31 passed across service/native/vec-index suites.
  Production behavior unchanged; only the injected operation was exported.
- Loaded sqlite-vec v0.1.9 supports TEXT primary-key IN filtering inside KNN.
  Existing tables use L2; the production scoped scan uses cosine.
- Test-only exact blob-scan candidate verifies eligible index entries against
  authoritative JSON and falls back for missing/stale rows. It was slower than
  exact JSON SQL in all 12 completed N=1k/10k text/media scope cases.
- At N=10k broad scope, exact SQL p95 was 301.83ms text / 296.72ms media;
  candidate p95 was 465.08ms / 470.50ms. These exclude inference and UI.
- N=50k text/broad hit the 120s case deadline; the other five N=50k cases were not
  reached. No complete timings are claimed for them. Benchmark suite failed after
  a prior harness decoding repair, triggering the plan's STOP condition.
- Recommendation: keep the exact production scan; await approval to finalize the
  no-change decision and resolve benchmark protocol/gates. No schema/strategy
  change, no shared-runtime restart/switch, and no model downloads.
- Repository-wide gates have not been rerun for these plan 004 additions.
  See the decision report for commands, environment, limitations and acceptance
  proposal; no performance target or no-change decision approval is implied.

## Plan 004 approved finalization — 2026-10-30

User approved retaining exact retrieval and rejecting the test-only prototype.
[Final decision, full tables and raw records](vector-retrieval-decision.md#finalization-after-approval--2026-10-30).

Independent 120s phase budgets plus a 550s per-size workload cap yielded 18
records: 50/54 timed phases complete. The candidate was slower in all 16 fully
comparable workloads. At N=50k broad text, exact SQL p95 1416.27ms versus
2371.68ms candidate; media 1411.33ms versus 2372.68ms. These are synchronous
in-memory SQL measurements, not encoder or UI latency.

N=50k media 10% candidate and all three media 1% phases remain explicitly
incomplete due to the overall cap; no p95 values are claimed for them.
Correctness/fallback checks passed. The opt-in command exited 0 while reporting
these limitations rather than disguising them as complete performance results.

Final pnpm check/build passed (all size budgets); explicit native retrieval/
service/db/vec suite passed 34 tests without skips. The production strategy,
shared runtime, and personal Libraries remain unchanged. Plan 004 is REJECTED
with evidence, not an optimization shipped. No commits/pushes made.
